title: ISIS Supporter Calls For Creating Encrypted App For Supporters To Share Their Jihadi Content; Posts AI-Generated Videos Depicting White House Exploding, Threatening President Trump, Celebrating Charlie Kirk Assassination | MEMRI
text:
A user of a pro-ISIS encrypted platform published multiple English-language inciting posters and posts, saying he created them on his phone, using AI. He called for the creation of an encrupted application where ISIS supporters can share the content they create, as well as tips to improve their content. In his content, the user celebrated 9/11, the killing of Charlie Kirk, and threatened President Trump, depicting the White House being detonated.
On September 12, 2025, the user published graphics celebrating the killing of Charlie Kirk and warning that President Trump is "next". The next day, the user posted a video celebrating the 9/11 attacks, claiming ISIS is not an extremist or terrorist organization, and implying that the death of Charlie Kirk is a victory for ISIS. Another video depicted the White House exploding, with an ISIS flag, and President Trump depicted in what may be pajamas or a prison uniform.
That same day, the user shared a series of posters with tips for online safety for other jihadis. He recommended the use of Lumo, an encrypted AI chat service provided by the Swiss company Proton Technologies, highlighting its end-to-end and zero-access encryption for "complete privacy" and praising it for not being owned by an American company, citing "transparency and trust." The user asked other supporters for advice on how to establish his own channel on the platform to expand the reach of his content.
Click below to view the video showing the White House exploding:
https://www.memri.org/jttm/isis-supporter-publishes-graphics-and-videos-inciting-attacks-president-trump-detonating-white#
On September 15, 2025, the user posted another self-produced video, saying it was created using AI. The video depicted ISIS fighters using weapons in a desert landscape. Discussing the video with other supporters on the platform, the user said he created the video on his phone, using free sound effects and background sounds. He then called on others develop a secure community app where ISIS supporters can share content they make and advise others on improving their work, recommending tools. He proposed that the app work like the encrypted app Session, using the encrypted Tor browser.
